risks.risk: Wrong gearbox type/fitment (e.g., different Ford Fusion transmission variant) leading to mismatch with the buyer’s engine and wiring/shift components.
risks.proof: Photo of the gearbox identification tag/label (part number) and/or the transmission code stamped on the casing, plus a photo of the bellhousing/connector side.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: not guaranteed to fit (treated as for parts / needs verification before installation).

risks.risk: Condition risk: internal damage or incomplete rebuild (photos show a removed unit but do not confirm operation).
risks.proof: Video clip of the gearbox being tested (engaged in gear / fluid pressure test) or a short bench test with fluid and output rotation.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: not working / unknown condition.

risks.risk: Missing components (sensors, solenoids, torque converter, linkage, bolts) that are not visible in the photos.
risks.proof: Photo checklist: all external sensors/ports, torque converter mating surface, and what exact parts are included in the package.
risks.if_unproven: Price as worst-case: may be missing parts.

risks.risk: Fluid leaks or cracked casing not visible from these angles.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of seams, drain/plug areas, and any cracks; wipe-clean then show fresh leak-free condition.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the transmission ID plate/label and any stamped transmission code/part number on the casing (both sides if possible).
Send a video of the gearbox being tested (output shaft rotation/engagement) or a bench test result.
Confirm what is included: torque converter (if applicable), sensors/solenoids, wiring connectors, and any external brackets/bolts.
Provide close-ups of the bellhousing mating surface and any ports to confirm nothing is broken or missing.
response.reason: The photos show a gearbox/transmission assembly, but there is no readable part number or fitment code to confirm it matches a Ford Fusion 4-cylinder application, and the condition cannot be verified from images alone. Proof is needed before a reliable worst-case price can be set.
